time_scope: modern literary Kalmyk described from mid-20th-century sources
claim: Kalmyk has word-level front/back (palatal) vowel harmony: vowels in a harmonic word are front or back, with /i/ neutral in its segmental quality.
normalized_environment: word vowels agree in front/back harmony class; i does not alternate in quality
scope: literary Kalmyk as treated in Svantesson's West Mongolian comparison
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The source distinguishes Kalmyk from East Mongolian systems whose phonetic harmony basis shifted; this record is lect-specific and does not generalize across Mongolic.
section: 4 West Mongolian / Kalmyk vowel harmony discussion

time_scope: modern literary Kalmyk described from mid-20th-century sources
claim: The first vowel of a Kalmyk word determines its harmony class; crucially, initial /i/ selects the front-harmonic class even though /i/ is otherwise neutral in the harmony alternation.

source_forms.initial_i: word with first vowel i is front harmonic
source_forms.comparison: Classical Mongolian instead lets initial neutral i coexist with either harmony class

exceptions_or_counterexamples: Svantesson notes dialectal differences within Oirat and historical cases in which earlier initial /i/ was assimilated to a following vowel, leaving the word back-harmonic; the literary Kalmyk generalization is therefore not projected to every Oirat dialect or historical input.
section: 4 West Mongolian / Kalmyk vowel harmony discussion

time_scope: modern literary Kalmyk described from mid-20th-century sources
claim: Kalmyk suffix vowels have two front/back harmonic forms, with no productive rounding-harmony alternation in the system described; /i/ remains invariant.

source_forms.suffix_allomorphy: two alternating forms according to front/back class

normalized_environment: suffix V alternates for palatal harmony only; no rounding-harmony series
scope: suffixal vowel alternations in literary Kalmyk
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The claim is specific to the Kalmyk system described by Svantesson and contrasts with Mongolic varieties that have different harmony systems.
